monthly_review.summary: You've increased volume and intensity this month, with faster average pace and higher aerobic training effect, but cadence dipped slightly and efficiency improved marginally.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite 4 fewer runs and 9.4 km less volume than last month, your average pace improved by 20 sec/km while average HR rose 4 bpm — indicating a meaningful shift toward higher-intensity work.

goal_tracker.message: You need 9.4 more km across 4 remaining sessions to match last month's volume — averaging 2.4 km per session. Given your recent long runs (12.0 km and 14.1 km), you can easily achieve this with one additional medium run (6–8 km) and three shorter maintenance runs (2–3 km each).

insights.title: Efficiency is trending upward despite pace increase
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency improved from 13.46 to 13.52 km/hr per bpm — a small but real gain — even as average pace quickened and HR rose, suggesting better cardiovascular economy at higher intensities.

insights.title: Zone 3 and Zone 4 dominance signals growing threshold focus
insights.body: This month’s HR zone distribution shows 27% in Zone 3 and 19% in Zone 4 — up from 31% Zone 3 and 15% Zone 4 last month — reflecting a deliberate, measurable shift toward lactate threshold and VO2 max stimulus.

insights.title: Cadence variability correlates with fatigue and terrain
insights.body: Cadence dropped to 135–136 spm on slower, higher-ground-contact runs (e.g., 4.0 km @ 129 bpm, ground contact 300 ms; and 4.1 km @ 141 bpm, ground contact 312 ms), while hitting 151–153 spm on fresher or longer efforts — suggesting form degrades under cumulative load or low-HR endurance effort.

insights.title: Long-run frequency increased but recovery may be compressed
insights.body: You completed two 12+ km runs in the last 6 days (14.1 km on 7/12 and 12.0 km on 7/17), yet only one run under 2 km since 7/6 — no true easy/recovery run in that stretch, reflected in rising avg HR (+4 bpm) and reduced cadence.

recommendations.action: Do a 5.0 km Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm) within next 48 hours, focusing on cadence ≥148 spm and ground contact <305 ms
recommendations.reason: Your last two short runs had cadence ≤136 spm and ground contact ≥300 ms — this session will reinforce neuromuscular efficiency and active recovery without adding stress.

recommendations.action: Insert a 2.0 km barefoot or minimalist-shoe drill session (stride length focus: aim for +3 cm vs current 70–86 cm range) on soft surface
recommendations.reason: Stride length collapsed to 70.4 cm on both 12.0 km and 14.1 km runs — below your 85–89 cm range on easier efforts — signaling fatigue-induced gait shortening needing targeted retraining.

recommendations.action: Perform 3 × 3-min progressive strides post-run (starting at 5:30/km, ending at 4:55/km), with full 90-sec walk recovery between
recommendations.reason: Your best recent pace is 475 sec/km (7:55/km), but your 7/15 run at 8:30/km (510 sec/km) showed aerobic TE 3.1 — these strides will safely bridge pace gaps while reinforcing neuromuscular coordination without elevating HR into Zone 4.

weekly_focus.description: Prioritize neuromuscular refresh and HR-controlled pacing to reset cadence consistency and prevent further ground contact creep — especially after two back-to-back long runs.
suggested_sessions: 5 km Zone 2 tempo (HR ≤135 bpm, cadence ≥148 spm)
2 km form-focused strides + mobility drill circuit
6 km conversational Zone 2 (HR 128–134 bpm, vertical oscillation ≤7.5 cm)
